| Q | Key | Difficulty / syllabus relevance | Clinical audit result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | D | Medium, asthma assessment | Silent chest with exhaustion is emergency, not improvement. |
| 8 | C | Medium, pulse oximetry | Check poor perfusion and reliable site, never delay emergency care for a reading. |
| 9 | C | Medium, breath sounds | Local grating sound supports pleural rub. |
| 10 | B | Difficult, spirometry diagnostic application | TLC confirms additional restriction, advanced interpretation flagged as enrichment. |
| 11 | A | Easy, bronchoscopy aftercare | Protect swallowing and airway before oral intake, distractors are straightforward. |
| 12 | D | Easy, thoracentesis nursing | Usual upright forward position, individualized if not tolerated. |
| 13 | D | Medium, asthma control | Repeated SABA during worsening requires prompt review, ICS-containing management and action plan. |
| 14 | C | Easy, ICS teaching | Rinse and spit after maintenance ICS, existing thrush needs review. |
| 15 | B | Medium, COPD assessment | ABG detects CO2, drowsiness warrants urgent assessment not waiting for ABG. |
| 16 | A | Medium, inhaler technique | Match DPI inspiratory requirement to patient ability. |
| 17 | A | Easy, COPD nutrition | Small frequent meals and rest, individualized diet. |
| 18 | D | Difficult, COPD respiratory failure | Bilevel NIV appropriate if suitable, monitor and escalate if failing. |
